1970 Detektiv Sahnasi

Yomg‘irli tunda ofisda ochilayotgan fitna — 5 kadrli kinematografik ketma-ketlik uchun tayyor promptlar va yakuniy video natija.

Qanday ishlatiladi: referens rasmni yuklang, quyidagi 5 ta promptni tartib bilan (1→5) bering. Har bir kadr 3–5 soniyalik. Har bir prompt yonidagi “Nusxa” tugmasi orqali matnni to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri nusxalab olishingiz mumkin. Eng oxirida — shu promptlar asosida tayyorlangan video natija.

Kadrlar bo‘yicha promptlar

1

Ochilish — Ziddiyat

Medium two-shot · 3s

Use the reference image as the exact character and office reference. Same faces, clothing, 1970s detective office and rainy night.

Harakat

3-second cinematic medium two-shot. The female detective suddenly places a witness report on the desk and points at two conflicting times. She looks frustrated but controlled. The man studies the document silently.

Kamera

Camera slowly pushes toward the desk. Warm desk-lamp light illuminates the report while cold blue rain light enters through the window.

Female detective (sharply) “These times don’t match the witness statement.”

Natural body movement, realistic lip sync, tense atmosphere.

2

Guvoh yolg‘on gapirgan

Over-the-shoulder · 3s

Same characters, office, clothing and rainy-night continuity.

Harakat

3-second over-the-shoulder shot from behind the woman, focused on the male detective. He leans forward, takes the report and taps the witness signature with his pen. His expression becomes confident and suspicious.

Kamera

Slow sideways camera movement. Half of his face remains in shadow while the desk lamp highlights his eyes.

Male detective (firmly) “Because the witness lied.”

Restrained anger, natural hand movement, cinematic realism.

3

O‘zgartirilgan hisobot

Close-up · 3s

Same exact characters and environment.

Harakat

3-second close-up on the female detective. She quickly opens another case file and compares the original report with a carbon copy. Her eyes narrow as she notices different handwriting.

Kamera

Camera tilts from the papers up to her face. A passing car outside briefly sends moving light across her eyes.

Female detective (argues) “No. Someone changed the report.”

Serious expression, controlled breathing, subtle tension in her hands.

4

Ofisga kim kira olgan?

Low-angle CU · 3s

Same character identities and 1970s detective office.

Harakat

3-second low-angle medium close-up of the male detective. He stands slightly from his chair, places both hands on the desk and looks toward the locked office door. His confidence changes into alarm.

Kamera

Slow dramatic dolly-in. The desk lamp flickers subtly as thunder flashes through the rainy window.

Male detective (quietly) “Then the killer had access to this office.”

Natural movement, tense pause, realistic fear hidden beneath professional control.

5

Fitna fosh bo‘ladi

Cinematic close-up · 3s

Same characters, clothing, lighting and office continuity.

Harakat

3-second cinematic close-up of the female detective. She slides an old photograph across the desk, revealing the police captain standing beside the main suspect. She looks directly at the man, calm but disturbed.

Kamera

Camera tracks with the photograph, then racks focus onto her face. Lightning briefly brightens the room before it falls back into warm darkness.

Female detective (slowly) “Not the killer… our captain.”

End with both detectives silently realizing the conspiracy.

Umumiy prompt (butun sahna uchun)

Use the provided reference image as the exact character, wardrobe, environment and mood reference.

Create a cinematic 5-shot detective sequence set in a 1970s private investigation office at night during heavy rain. The scene must look like it was taken from a real feature film, not like a staged photoshoot. Preserve the same two detectives throughout all shots: the same man and woman from the reference image, with the same facial identity, hairstyle, age, clothing style and overall appearance.

They are sitting in their office late at night, working on a major criminal case and arguing while solving a difficult mystery. The emotional tone is tense, intelligent, serious and suspenseful. Their conversation should feel sharp, realistic and dramatic, as if they are slowly uncovering a dangerous conspiracy.

The office should feel authentic to the 1970s: paper files, folders, desk clutter, a practical desk lamp, analog objects, muted brown and amber tones, subtle cigarette-smoke atmosphere, old wood textures, and rain-covered windows behind them. Outside the window, heavy rain must be visible, with soft city lights and occasional passing reflections. The room should be in color, not black and white, but should still carry a classic noir-inspired cinematic mood.

Lighting must support the emotion of the dialogue: warm desk-lamp light on their faces, mixed with cooler rainy window light from behind or from the side. Use realistic cinematic contrast, moody shadows, subtle reflections, and natural film-like color grading. During more intense lines, use slightly more dramatic light contrast or a subtle flicker from the lamp or lightning glow outside.

Camera work must feel professional and story-driven. Across the sequence, vary the camera angles naturally: medium two-shot, over-the-shoulder shot, close-up, low-angle dramatic shot, and detail-driven reveal shot. Use slow cinematic push-ins, slight lateral slides, tilt-ups from evidence to faces, and gentle rack focus between the clues and the detectives. Camera movement must remain smooth, restrained and elegant.

The characters must move naturally and emotionally. Their face expressions, eye movements, hand gestures, posture shifts and breathing should match the seriousness of the conversation. The man should feel analytical, suspicious and increasingly alarmed. The woman should feel sharp, observant, controlled and quietly intense. Their body language should reflect rising tension as they examine documents, compare evidence, point at inconsistencies, and realize the truth.

The sequence should build from disagreement to revelation: - first, they argue over a contradiction in the evidence; - then they suspect the witness lied; - then a modified report is discovered; - then they realize the criminal had access to their office; - finally, they uncover that someone inside the police structure is connected to the crime.

Dialogue must feel grounded, cinematic and serious. Natural lip sync is required. The scene must end with both detectives realizing that the conspiracy is bigger than they expected.

Important constraints: Keep the same two characters in every shot. Keep the same office and same rainy-night continuity. No extra people entering the frame. No subtitles or on-screen text. No exaggerated acting. No modern props. No visual distortion. No cartoon look. No black-and-white output.

The final result must feel like a suspenseful 1970s detective thriller scene from a real movie.
